title: dev-platform-onramp-friction-map-and-pricing-drafts
summary: Messaging brief aimed at platform and backend engineers: emphasize predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and zero-surprise scaling. Includes quickstart angle for teams that need to go from signup to validated integration in under an hour, plus three pricing-language variants to A/B test on the sign-up and docs funnels.
objective: Create a concise set of developer-first hooks and copy snippets (homepage, quickstart, docs badges) that highlight Redwood Hosted API as the predictable, low-friction inference path for platform teams and product engineers. Provide pricing language drafts that balance clarity (per-token economics) with value-based tiers for committed customers.
target_audiences: Platform engineers at mid-market SaaS (need predictable latency & multi-tenant isolation)
ML engineers prototyping feature rollouts (care about latency SLOs and cost transparency)
Startup dev teams doing rapid experiments (first integration in 30–60 minutes)
DevOps and infra teams evaluating SLA/backoff options for inference endpoints
core_value_props: Turnkey low-latency inference: 95th percentile latency SLOs, transparent perf tradeoffs by model/sequence length
Predictable unit economics: per-token pricing plus clear reserved commitment options for Dedicated
Seamless migration path: same API surface for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
Developer ergonomics: minimal client setup, streaming responses, and drop-in SDKs with examples
quickstart_angle_steps: 0. Sign up and create key: emphasize sample key creation UI (30s)
1. Install SDK: npm/pip one-liner and echo-based test (1 min)
2. Make a single generate call against a tiny model: show JSON body and response streaming (2–3 min)
3. Swap to production model: demonstrate model param and token budget controls (5 min)
4. Add batch/kv cache hint: short example to reduce per-token costs (5–10 min)
Goal: developer feels confident to ship a first API call in <10 minutes and a validated flow in <60 minutes
hero_microcopy_options: Launch inference fast — predictable latency, transparent costs.
From prototype to production: one API, consistent performance.
Build fast. Serve reliably. Pay clearly.
High-performance LLM inference for engineers who measure latency and cost.
pricing_language_variants: Variant A (unit-first): 'Per-token pricing with clear sample invoices — $0.01/1K tokens for small models, discounts with monthly committed spend. No hidden fees; cost breakdown in Console.'
Variant B (commit-first): 'Reserved tiers for predictable throughput — Developer, Team, Enterprise. Commit monthly to lower unit price and unlock burst capacity and improved SLOs.'
Variant C (hybrid): 'Pay-as-you-go for fast experiments, reserve capacity when you need predictability. Console suggests optimal mix based on traffic patterns.'
competitor_takes: General cloud endpoints: reliable infra but large cognitive overhead (model packaging + ops). Our angle: same ease as managed endpoints with inference-tuned runtime and dev ergonomics.

LLM API incumbents (broad model providers): excellent demo speed; weaker on predictable unit economics and enterprise routing. Our angle: explicit cost/latency controls + fallbacks to cheaper variants.
Self-hosted runtimes: ultimate control but heavy ops and longer TTR. Our angle: offer private deployments with optional customer-managed infra for teams who want both control and plug-and-play UX.
Inference-focused vendors: good at throughput; fewer developer UX niceties (SDKs, quickstarts, streaming). Our angle: combine high-throughput runtime with best-in-class developer experience.
launch_experiments_and_metrics: A/B test homepage hero: Variant A vs Variant C microcopy; measure click-through to quickstart and avg time-to-first-api-call
Docs banner pricing language test: unit-first vs commit-first; measure conversion from free credits to paid plan within 14 days
Quickstart flow optimization: measure median time from signup to first successful generate call; target <10 minutes for 60%+ of signups
Instrument Console UX: surface predicted monthly spend given example prompts; metric: % of teams who view cost breakdown before making production calls
open_questions: What are our exact 95th percentile latency targets by model family for marketing copy? (need SRE confirmation)
Should pricing copy show concrete numbers on homepage or keep ranges to avoid hard promises? Legal prefers ranges for public pages.
Do we need an explicit 'try low-cost variant' CTA in quickstart for cost-sensitive experiments?
What SLA language is safe to show for Hosted vs Dedicated in public docs?
notes: Draft tone: conversational but precise — this doc is for dev-focused site copy and quickstart snippets. Keep technical details high-level in marketing materials, but link to detailed SLO/perf pages for engineers who want the numbers. Follow-up: sync with SRE to confirm latency buckets, and with Pricing for final commit discount tiers. Recommended immediate next step: implement Variant C pricing banner in staging docs and run a two-week test targeted at signups created from developer tutorials.
